audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht Biology studies living systems from molecules and cells to organisms and ecosystems. The first year covers molecular biology, plants, microorganisms, animals, evolution, ecology, genomics and statistics. Later Biology electives allow students to develop an emphasis before completing a supervised research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The broad UCR option connects cellular biology and physiology to evolution and ecology. One focused option adds disease, neuroscience and computational methods. The other adds conservation and studies how climate and human activity change ecosystems. Utrecht includes dedicated plant physiology and genome analysis and requires a 15 EC Biology research project.

curriculum.limitation: This outline preserves the restricted Biology electives and the 45 EC of profiling space. Utrecht’s study-interest directions guide choices within one Biology degree.

componentNotes.bio-y1-choice: Choose Biotechnologie en maatschappij or Introductie Mariene wetenschappen.
componentNotes.bio-major-choice: Across the 60 EC of Biology electives, complete at least 15 EC at level 2 and 30 EC at level 3, including at least 22.5 EC from the designated level 3* courses.
componentNotes.bio-graduation: Entry requires 120 EC within the Biology major, including the compulsory first-year courses and Academic Communication. Profiling courses fall outside these 120 EC.
componentNotes.bio-profiling: At least 15 of these 45 EC must be at level 2 or 3. This space can include individual electives or a minor.

notes.text: Utrecht combines a broad compulsory first year with restricted Biology electives and a 15 EC graduation project. UCR offers substantial overlap in cell biology, genetics, physiology, ecology and quantitative methods. Utrecht gives more dedicated attention to plant physiology and genome analysis. Its required research project differs from UCR’s team sustainability project and optional independent research.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

HCBGATE101.text: Introduces the molecular and cellular foundations of life and biomedical science. Topics include biological molecules, cells and membranes, communication, metabolism, cell division, heredity, gene expression and biotechnology. Students analyse scientific experiments and papers through teaching contributions and a research-based mini-symposium, with additional topics selected with the class.

ENSDELT312.name: Governance of Sustainability
ENSDELT312.text: This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.

ENSSUST313.name: Research in a Sustainable Delta
ENSSUST313.text: In this project course you will work in small teams of two or three students on a research problem relevant for sustainability in the broadest sense. We are looking for collaborations with local companies and other institutions. In this way it is guaranteed that the research projects are indeed relevant for the Zeeland delta.
